threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look shocked when you hear a tube strike's on. The locals just nod and carry on, like it's the weather.
Got on the 36 last night and a bloke was deep into a heated debate with a bag of chips. The chips won, but he didn't even flinch. Classic Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I found someone selling homemade Mutzen on the corner every Saturday, just like my grandma used to. It feels like a real community.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find abandoned subway stations here, like
Pankstraße: - hidden gems where you can still feel the city's history.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their disdain for the BART delays—when the train's late, we know to grab tacos first, then check for updates.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy at the Muni stop trying to trade his skateboard for coffee. The barista looked confused, but hey, it’s San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s park benches are for picnics; locals know they’re for people-watching, especially during the evening hours.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their eagerness to ask for directions at every turn, even when the Metro entrance is just steps away.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the tube is on strike—locals just grab a bike or walk, and carry on like it's a sunny day.
Last night on the 133, a bloke serenaded the driver with an off-key rendition of 'Wonderwall' while everyone tried to ignore him. Pure Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I found my favorite kebab shop still open at 3 AM, with the owner sharing stories about every late-night customer.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find techno parties in abandoned buildings that last all weekend, complete with makeshift bars and old couches to crash on.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by their instinct to grab a burrito in hand, even if they’re late for BART; tourists just stare at the menu.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 at 5:15, driver stopped for a street performer doing backflips. Crowd laughed, he took a bow, then we all packed in like sardines.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always ask for the best tapas bar, but they miss the tiny bodegas where locals actually grab a quick vermut. That's where the real vibe is.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newbie by the way they stop at every crosswalk, waiting for the light, while locals just zip across without a second thought.
